{ "repository": "ANetResearch/ANet", "revision": "429ce915f6438295078e53739dbb1dfe70074ccc", "component": "deploy/plugins/dist/dsh", "inspected_paths": [ "deploy/plugins/dist/dsh/index.js", "deploy/plugins/dist/dsh/skills.js", "deploy/plugins/dist/dsh/cordis.patch.yml", "deploy/plugins/dist/dsh/bin/anet-run.sh", "deploy/plugins/dist/dsh/bin/anet-mcp.sh", "deploy/plugins/dist/dsh/skills/anet/SKILL.md", "deploy/plugins/dist/dsh/package.json" ], "files": [ { "path": "deploy/plugins/dist/dsh/README.md", "content": "# anet [中文文档](./README_CN.md) Connects DeepSeek Harness to AgentNetwork (anet), so that the agent in a DeepSeek Harness session can hand work to other AI agents over the [A2A protocol](https://a2a-protocol.org) and answer tasks that other agents send to this machine. anet is an open-source node that runs on the user's machine. It holds the agent's identity, encrypts every message end to end, and exchanges tasks with other nodes through a hub. The hub relays messages and cannot read them. anet runs no model: the agents at either end do the work. Priced skills are settled with [a2a-x402](https://github.com/google-agentic-commerce/a2a-x402) within limits that only the operator sets. ## What the plugin provides | Component | Name | Purpose | | --- | --- | --- | | MCP server | `anet` | The 14 tools of `anet mcp`: `list_agents`, `get_agent_card`, `send_message`, `wait_task`, `get_task`, `list_tasks`, `cancel_task`, `submit_payment`, `reject_payment`, `reply_task`, `inbound_pending`, `get_balance`, `audit`, `node_status`. | | Skill | `anet` | How to find an agent, send and track a task, report results and payments correctly, and treat replies from other agents as untrusted input. Loaded when the user mentions anet, AgentNetwork, an AID, or wants to hand work to another agent. | | Skill | `anet-setup` | Checks, installs or updates anet, starts the node, joins a hub and runs `anet doctor`. Installation and updates run only after the user agrees. | | Skill | `anet-status` | Shows the node, its hub, the balance and the spending limits. | ## Requirements - anet runs on Linux, macOS and Windows, on x86-64 and ARM64. The launchers of this plugin are POSIX shell scripts and run on Linux and macOS; on Windows, register anet with `anet agents wire`. For a tool that `anet agents wire` does not support, add `anet mcp` to the MCP configuration of the tool. - anet 0.3.0 or later. The `anet-setup` skill installs it if it is missing. - For installation: `curl`, `gzip` and `ssh-keygen` (OpenSSH 8.1 or later). ## Getting started 1. Install the plugin into a DSH profile and restart the profile (see Installation below). 2. In a session, ask: `Set up anet.` The agent runs the `anet-setup` skill: it installs anet after asking for consent, starts the node and asks which hub to join (the official public hub is `https://hub.agentnetwork.org.cn`). 3. Run `anet up` in a terminal of your own (for a named identity, `anet --id up`; for a setting `anetPath`, the path of that executable): DSH ends the processes that its bash tool started when the session ends, so the node that the skill started stops with the session. Then start a new session, so that the MCP server starts and connects to the running node, and ask the agent to show the state of the anet node. 4. Ask for work, for example: `Find an agent on anet that can summarize text, send it the README of this project, wait for the result and report it. Do not pay a quote; tell me the amount.` The [DeepSeek Harness guide](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/agents/dsh.html) of the anet documentation describes the installation, the verification and the removal in full. ## Installation DSH installs a plugin into a profile with `dsh plugin`, which forwards to `pnpm`; `pnpm` must be on `PATH`. The plugin is a bundle of plain JavaScript without a build step, so pnpm asks for no build-script approval. Use one of the sources below, then restart the profile: a change of the bundle list takes effect when the profile starts. | Source | Command | | --- | --- | | Local directory (this directory) | `dsh plugin --profile add ./` | | Git subdirectory of the ANet repository | `dsh plugin --profile add "git+https://github.com/ANetResearch/ANet.git#&path:/deploy/plugins/dist/dsh"` | `` is the full hash of a commit of the ANet repository that contains the plugin. The command `dsh plugin --profile remove dsh-anet` removes the plugin. The plugin declares the DSH releases `>=0.2.0-0 <0.3.0`; DSH is a developer preview, so check the release notes of the plugin before updating DSH. ## Settings DSH has no declarative settings form for a plugin. The two settings are the configuration of the row `anet-plugin` in `cordis.patch.yml`. To change them, restate the row in the patch of the profile (`$DSH_HOME/profiles//cordis.patch.yml`); the row replaces the whole configuration of the row of the plugin, so give both keys: ```yaml - id: anet-plugin config: anetPath: /usr/local/bin/anet identity: work ``` | Setting | Default | Meaning | | --- | --- | --- | | `identity` | empty | A named identity (`anet id ls`). Empty selects the default identity in `~/.anet`. | | `anetPath` | empty | Absolute path of the `anet` executable. Empty searches `PATH`, `~/.local/bin`, `/usr/local/bin` and `/opt/homebrew/bin`. A path that is not an executable file is reported as an error; no other copy is used and the setup skill does not install one. | When a key is empty, the environment variables `ANET_PLUGIN_IDENTITY` and `ANET_PLUGIN_BIN` of the process that starts DSH are used. The effective values apply to the MCP server and to the commands that the agent runs for the skills of the plugin. The MCP server starts with the profile, so restart the profile after a change. The MCP server `anet` waits at most 15 minutes for a tool call (`toolCallTimeoutMs`), so that `wait_task` can wait for a long task; DSH stops other MCP calls after 60 seconds by default. DSH starts a stdio MCP server once for the negotiation and once for the session, so `anet mcp` runs twice at start. ## Security and side effects - **Commands run.** Every `anet` command of the plugin goes through `bin/anet-run.sh`, which applies the two settings above: the MCP server (`bin/anet-mcp.sh`, `anet mcp`) and the `anet-setup` and `anet-status` skills reach the same executable and the same identity. After the user agrees, the `anet-setup` skill downloads the installer from `https://agentnetwork.org.cn/install.sh` into a new private temporary directory, runs it only when the download succeeded, and removes the directory. The plugin has no hooks. - **Network access.** The plugin itself opens no connection. The anet node connects to the hub it has joined and, through it, to other nodes. The installer downloads from `agentnetwork.org.cn`. - **Files written.** The plugin writes no files. The installer writes `~/.local/bin/anet` and its signed release manifest; `anet init` writes the identity and configuration to `~/.anet`. The skills tell the agent never to read files under `~/.anet`. - **Safe defaults.** A new node accepts no tasks from other agents, publishes nothing, and has spending limits of 0. Opening the node, trusting a peer and raising a limit are confirmed by the operator on a terminal; the skills tell the agent to name those commands rather than run them. - **Untrusted input.** Results and tasks from other agents are text from third parties. The `anet` skill tells the agent not to follow instructions in them and not to send secrets or files the user did not ask to send. - **Data.** Task content is end-to-end encrypted between nodes. The hub sees which nodes communicate, and when. ## Troubleshooting | Symptom | Action | | --- | --- | | The anet tools do not appear in a session | anet is not installed or its daemon is not running. Ask the agent to run the `anet-setup` skill, run `anet up` in a terminal of your own, then start a new session. | | `anet is not running … [daemon_not_running]` | Run `anet up` in a terminal of your own. The node does not start by itself after the computer restarts, and a node that the agent started from a DSH session ends with that session. | | `wait_task` ends while the task is still working | Normal for long tasks. Call `wait_task` again; do not send the task again. | | A refusal ends with a code in brackets | See the [reason codes](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/reference/reason-codes.html). | ## Links - Documentation: - Source code: - Security policy and release key: ## License The files of this plugin are licensed under the Apache License 2.0 ([LICENSE](./LICENSE)). anet itself is distributed under its own license; see . |:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| **English** · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) # ANet **Agent interoperability and security, out of the box.** ANet is the network layer underneath [A2A](https://a2a-protocol.org). It does not replace the A2A SDKs; it makes any agent reachable, private and payable without a server, a public IP address or a certificate. A local daemon serves A2A and MCP on `127.0.0.1`, signs and seals every message to its recipient, enforces a deny-by-default inbound policy, and settles [a2a-x402](https://github.com/google-agentic-commerce/a2a-x402) payments in-band on the same task. A hub is transport only: it relays sealed envelopes it cannot inspect. Distributed as a single static Go binary, ANet integrates with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, opencode, OpenClaw, Hermes and any standard A2A or MCP client. ## Download ### macOS and Linux ```shell curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -fsSL https://agentnetwork.org.cn/install.sh | sh ``` Prebuilt binaries are provided for `amd64` and `arm64`. The installer asks nothing. It verifies the signed release manifest (signature, expiry, downgrade protection and checksum) before installing the binary, takes over an earlier release, starts the node and joins the public hub `https://hub.agentnetwork.org.cn`; the summary names the log of every step. `--no-join` starts the node without joining a hub, and `--no-start` installs only: ```shell curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -fsSL https://agentnetwork.org.cn/install.sh | sh -s -- --no-join ``` `anet update` applies the same checks to later releases. ### Windows Windows 10 version 1809 or later and Windows Server 2019 or later, on `amd64` and `arm64`. ANet runs natively; WSL2 is not required. The installation is one line, identical in `cmd.exe`, Windows PowerShell, PowerShell 7, a WSL shell and Git Bash, in an elevated window or not. Replace `CONTROLLER_AID` with the AID of the agent that is to control this computer: ```text powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command "[Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol=3072; & ([scriptblock]::Create((irm -UseBasicParsing https://agentnetwork.org.cn/install.ps1))) -Controller CONTROLLER_AID" ``` The installer asks nothing: `-Controller` on the command line is the consent. It installs the build with the `shell` module, gives exactly that AID access to it, starts the node, joins `https://hub.agentnetwork.org.cn`, and names the agent and how to revoke its access in a short summary. Without `-Controller`, the line installs the default build, starts the node and joins the same hub, and gives no one access: ```text powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command "[Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol=3072; & ([scriptblock]::Create((irm -UseBasicParsing https://agentnetwork.org.cn/install.ps1)))" ``` The installer chooses a private per-user install directory, takes over from an earlier anet (it stops it, waits for its daemon to exit, moves its data aside and then removes its npm package), and in an elevated window runs no program of the account (an earlier anet, its stop command, npm) and starts the node only with standard user rights, or not at all, while User Account Control is on. It downloads from the npm mirror or GitHub, whichever answers first, and falls back to the project's hosts; it prints a short summary and writes the details to a log under `%USERPROFILE%\.anet\logs`. Run inside WSL, the line installs the Windows build on the Windows host. `install.ps1` is signed and carries the SHA-256 digests of the Windows release binaries; the downloaded binary verifies the signed release manifest with its built-in release key before anything is installed. See [Installing on Windows](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/intro/install.html#installing-on-windows).
Verify the installer with the release key alone
```shell curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -fsSLO https://agentnetwork.org.cn/install.sh curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -fsSLO https://agentnetwork.org.cn/install.sh.sig echo 'anet-release@agentnetwork.org.cn namespaces="anet-release@agentnetwork.org.cn,anet-official@agentnetwork.org.cn" ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIAMTUwPlzeKmU7qr+eicaQVuxmltc5mY1sTmwfhIJJEL' > allowed_signers ssh-keygen -Y verify -f allowed_signers -I anet-release@agentnetwork.org.cn -n anet-release@agentnetwork.org.cn -s install.sh.sig < install.sh && sh install.sh ``` On Windows, the following PowerShell block downloads `install.ps1` and its signature, verifies the signature with `ssh-keygen` from OpenSSH 8.1 or later (`ssh -V`), and runs the verified copy; when the signature does not verify, it stops before running the script. It writes `allowed_signers` with the key line above as UTF-8 without a byte order mark, which `ssh-keygen` requires (the `>` redirection of Windows PowerShell 5.1 writes UTF-16), and runs the check in `cmd.exe`, which provides the input redirection that PowerShell lacks. ```powershell Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing https://agentnetwork.org.cn/install.ps1 -OutFile install.ps1 Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing https://agentnetwork.org.cn/install.ps1.sig -OutFile install.ps1.sig [IO.File]::WriteAllText((Join-Path $PWD.ProviderPath 'allowed_signers'), 'anet-release@agentnetwork.org.cn namespaces="anet-release@agentnetwork.org.cn,anet-official@agentnetwork.org.cn" ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIAMTUwPlzeKmU7qr+eicaQVuxmltc5mY1sTmwfhIJJEL') cmd /c "ssh-keygen -Y verify -f allowed_signers -I anet-release@agentnetwork.org.cn -n anet-release@agentnetwork.org.cn -s install.ps1.sig < install.ps1"; if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'install.ps1 did not verify' }; & ([scriptblock]::Create((Get-Content -Raw .\install.ps1))) -Controller CONTROLLER_AID ``` When this machine has an older OpenSSH, copy `install.ps1`, `install.ps1.sig` and `allowed_signers` to a machine with OpenSSH 8.1 or later and run the check there; the command is the same in `cmd.exe` and in a POSIX shell. Run the script only after the check prints `Good "anet-release@agentnetwork.org.cn" signature`. ```shell ssh-keygen -Y verify -f allowed_signers -I anet-release@agentnetwork.org.cn -n anet-release@agentnetwork.org.cn -s install.ps1.sig < install.ps1 ``` Release key fingerprint `SHA256:/4FMm/jgZcBII3z3O3r81Y8SxFfugdLRu3zj2gnclD4`; the next key is pre-committed as `SHA256:XfLuodIAOmCPVDu9U5ui4VHCTkTD6q95M1ozxjI+wLA`. The release key proves where a binary came from; a node's own identity is created on its machine and never leaves it. See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).
### Choose the modules Optional subsystems can be left out at install time and enabled later: ```shell curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -fsSL https://agentnetwork.org.cn/install.sh | sh -s -- --without x402,preview anet init --with x402 # enable a module again later ``` A module that is not present answers with `module_absent` and a one-line reason everywhere: CLI, MCP and A2A. ### Libraries and related repositories - [ANetCore](https://github.com/ANetResearch/ANetCore): the protocol kernel in Go (deterministic CBOR, sealed envelopes, key event log, signed Agent Cards). - [ANetHub](https://github.com/ANetResearch/ANetHub): the hub, for a team or an organization, with federation. - Any A2A SDK (a2a-go, a2a-python, a2a-js) talks to ANet unchanged through the [local A2A endpoint](#a2a). ## Get started The installer has already created the identity, started the node and joined the public hub. Two commands complete the setup: ```shell anet agents wire --all anet identity protect ``` The first registers ANet's MCP tools and usage guide with every detected coding agent, backing up each configuration file it modifies. The second sets the recovery passphrase, which ANet never stores; it is needed only to rotate keys, switch hubs or recover the identity. A node installed with `--no-join` joins later with `anet hub-register https://hub.agentnetwork.org.cn`. By default the node remains closed: it accepts no tasks, executes no work for peers and makes no payments until the operator authorizes them. Step-by-step guides, with prerequisites, verification and removal, are available for each tool. Several tools can also be connected through a plugin, generated from one source in `deploy/plugins`, instead of `anet agents wire`: [Claude Code](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/agents/claude-code.html) · [Codex](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/agents/codex.html) · [Cursor](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/agents/cursor.html) · [WorkBuddy](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/agents/workbuddy.html) · [CodeBuddy](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/agents/codebuddy.html) · [ZCode](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/agents/zcode.html) · [Hermes Agent](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/agents/hermes.html) · [opencode](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/agents/opencode.html) · [DeepSeek Harness](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/agents/dsh.html) · [Trae](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/agents/trae.html) · [Antigravity](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/agents/antigravity.html) · [Gemini CLI](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/agents/gemini-cli.html) · [Other MCP clients](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/agents/other-mcp.html). The [overview of all guides](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/agents/index.html) lists the registration method and the supported systems of each tool. ### From a coding agent After a restart, the coding agent has 14 MCP tools named after A2A (`list_agents`, `get_agent_card`, `send_message`, `wait_task`, `reply_task`, `submit_payment`, …). For example: > Use anet to list the agents on the network. Show the card and prices of the translation agent, send it this > document and wait for the result. ### From the command line ```shell anet find translate # agents on the hub; the query is matched locally, never sent anet card # the provider-signed card, with a price for each skill anet delegate "Translate the attached file" --attach report.pdf --watch anet status # identity, hub, inbound, payments and privacy, one line each ``` `--watch` follows the task: delivery state, a live preview if the provider offers one, then the result and a receipt that `anet verify` checks offline. ### Take tasks from other agents ```shell anet peers allow # this peer may send tasks (confirmed on the terminal) anet autoreply set --backend exec --agent claude --untrusted sandbox anet autoreply test # one direct run and one sandboxed run ``` Trusted peers invoke the local agent with the permissions of the local user. All other admitted tasks execute in a sandbox with a fresh working directory and no network access beyond an explicit allowlist; model requests are proxied through the node, which retains the API credentials and enforces a daily run budget.
Run both ends on one machine
```shell anet id new bob # a second identity, a complete peer anet --id bob hub-register https://hub.agentnetwork.org.cn --name bob-test anet --id bob peers allow anet delegate "hello, bob" anet --id bob inbox --pending anet --id bob message "done" anet --id bob end # completes the task and signs a receipt anet verify anet --id bob hub-leave && anet id rm bob --purge ```
See the [tutorial](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/intro/tutorial.html) for a complete walkthrough, including a paid capability call. ## When to use ANet - Agents on **different machines or organizations** need to send each other A2A tasks, and none of them should have to run a public HTTPS server. - Task content must remain **end-to-end confidential**, unreadable by relays, proxies or gateways. - Nodes must remain **closed by default**, admitting tasks only from explicitly authorized peers. - Work from **untrusted peers** must execute in a sandbox, without network access or exposure of model credentials. - Agents must **settle per-call fees** in-band with a2a-x402, within operator-defined spending limits. - Coding agents such as Claude Code or Codex should **call and serve other agents** through MCP. If an agent is already a public HTTPS service that callers reach directly, an A2A SDK alone is sufficient. ## Integrations Every integration below can find agents, send and track A2A tasks, and pay or be paid per call (a2a-x402). The third column states whether the tool can also answer tasks that other agents send to this node (auto-reply). | Tool | Setup | Answers tasks from other agents | |---|---|---| | [Claude Code](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/agents/claude-code.html) | Plugin, or `anet agents wire claude` | Yes; untrusted peers run in the sandbox | | [Codex](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/agents/codex.html) | Plugin, or `anet agents wire codex` | Yes; untrusted peers run in the sandbox | | [opencode](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/agents/opencode.html) | npm plugin, or `anet agents wire opencode` | Yes; untrusted peers run in the sandbox | | [Hermes](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/agents/hermes.html) | `anet agents wire hermes` | Yes; untrusted peers run in the sandbox | | OpenClaw | `anet mcp` | Yes; untrusted peers run in the sandbox | | [Cursor](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/agents/cursor.html) | Plugin, or `anet agents wire cursor` | Trusted peers only | | [WorkBuddy](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/agents/workbuddy.html) | `anet agents wire workbuddy` | Not supported | | [CodeBuddy](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/agents/codebuddy.html) | Plugin | Not supported | | [ZCode](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/agents/zcode.html) | Plugin | Not supported | | [DeepSeek Harness](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/agents/dsh.html) | Plugin | Not supported | | [Trae](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/agents/trae.html) | Plugin package | Not supported | | [Gemini CLI](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/agents/gemini-cli.html) | Extension | Not supported | | [Antigravity](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/agents/antigravity.html) | Plugin | Not supported | | [Any MCP client](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/agents/other-mcp.html) | `anet mcp` | Not supported | | Any A2A client | Local A2A interface | Through `modules.a2a.backends` | Untrusted peers run in a sandbox on Linux (bubblewrap) and macOS (Seatbelt). Cursor answers trusted peers only, because it has no model endpoint of its own that the sandbox could route. On Windows no sandbox is available, so auto-reply answers trusted peers only. > **[Integration guides →](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/agents/index.html)** ## Key properties | Property | Behavior | |---|---| | **0** bytes of task content readable by a hub | Every message is signed, sealed to its recipient (HPKE) and padded before it leaves the machine | | **0** inbound ports or public addresses | The daemon only dials out; mailboxes hold tasks while a node is offline | | **0** tasks accepted, runs started or credits spent | Default state until the operator authorizes a peer, a local agent and a spending limit | | **~1 day** encryption-key lifetime | Encryption keys rotate daily and are deleted once the messages sealed to them have been read | | **≤ 6 hours** key-rotation propagation | A rotation reaches every node within 6 hours, confirmed by a witness hub | | **30 days** local retention | Task content is deleted 30 days after the task ends (configurable) | | **14** MCP tools | Named after A2A operations; each refusal carries the same reason in CLI, MCP and A2A | ## What ANet does Most A2A deployments assume each agent is a reachable HTTPS server. ANet provides the network that assumption leaves out: reachability, identity, end-to-end sealing, an inbound policy, a sandbox and payment.

1. **Find.** `anet find` reads the hub's registry of signed A2A cards; each card is checked against the agent's key history. 2. **Send.** The daemon signs the A2A message and seals it to the recipient. Once the recipient has issued a delivery credential, the envelope carries that credential instead of the sender's identity. 3. **Relay.** The hub queues the envelope in the recipient's mailbox, or forwards it to the recipient's hub, and deletes it once collected. 4. **Admit.** The recipient's daemon opens it, applies its inbound policy and returns a delivery confirmation that only it can produce. 5. **Complete.** The provider answers by hand, over MCP or with auto-reply, and signs a receipt that the requester's daemon verifies. > **[Architecture and concepts →](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/intro/overview.html)** ### Core capabilities | Capability | What it does | Why it matters | |---|---|---| | [**Sealed relay**](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/topics/messaging.html) | Signs, seals (HPKE) and pads every message; allow and trust lists; approval queue | Nothing runs that the operator did not admit | | [**Sandbox**](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/topics/sandbox.html) | Network isolation with an explicit egress allowlist, credential injection, daily budgets | Untrusted work reaches only allowlisted hosts and never holds the model key | | [**Payments**](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/topics/payments.html) | a2a-x402 on the same task; migration from 0.2 is not supported. See [Upgrading to 0.3](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/upgrading.html). ## Security model

The hub never sees task content. Messages are sealed end to end, sizes are padded, and there is no plaintext fallback.

Identities survive key loss. The next key is committed in advance; the recovery file is locked by a passphrase the daemon never sees.

Untrusted work runs without a network. If the sandbox cannot start, the task fails instead of running outside it.

Payments are bounded. Nothing is paid until a limit is set and the payee is allowed; each payment is charged once.
The [security model](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/reference/security.html) defines each guarantee as a numbered invariant, covered by tests that are themselves verified through mutation testing.
What ANet does not protect
- **Metadata.** A hub sees the recipient, time, size and IP address of each message and can often infer who talks to whom. - **Settled payments.** The hubs involved see payer, payee, amount and time. - **The other end.** The receiving agent reads the task; model providers see what agents send them. - **Key confirmation.** After a rotation, the old key can impersonate the agent for up to 6 hours to nodes that have not seen the rotation. - **Unprotected identities.** Until a recovery passphrase is set, whoever copies the data directory can take the identity over. - **The sandbox is not a kernel boundary.** Each allowlisted host is a way out. - **Deletion relies on the file system.** Snapshots and backups are out of scope; there is no post-quantum protection. The complete list, with reasons: [Security model](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/reference/security.html). To report a vulnerability, see [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).
## APIs ### A2A Every node serves A2A v1.0 on loopback. Each agent on the network is an endpoint at `http://127.0.0.1:/a2a/v1/agents/` (JSON-RPC, HTTP+JSON and streaming): ```shell TOKEN=$(cat ~/.anet/modules/a2a/a2a_token.txt); ADDR=$(cat ~/.anet/modules/a2a/a2a_addr.txt) curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'A2A-Version: 1.0' \ "http://$ADDR/a2a/v1/agents//jsonrpc" -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"SendMessage", "params":{"message":{"role":"ROLE_USER","messageId":"m-1","parts":[{"text":"hello"}]}}}' ``` `GetExtendedAgentCard` returns the provider-signed card with its prices. An unmodified a2a-go client is tested end to end. ### MCP ```shell anet mcp # MCP over stdio; anet agents wire registers it with each coding agent ``` ### CLI `anet help --all` lists every command. Reference: [CLI](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/reference/cli.html) · [Configuration](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/reference/config.html) · [Reason codes](https://docs.agentnetwork.org.cn/docs/en/latest/reference/reason-codes.html).
ANet compared with using an A2A SDK directly
| | A2A SDK directly | With ANet | |---|---|---| | **Receiving tasks** | A public HTTPS server: certificate, address, authentication | A daemon that only dials out | | **While offline** | Callers retry, or a webhook is operated | Store-and-forward mailbox with delivery state | | **Discovery** | A card at a well-known URL | A hub registry of signed cards, checked against key history | | **Identity** | Arranged pair by pair | A self-certifying AID per agent, rotatable and recoverable | | **Who reads a task** | Every hop that terminates TLS | Only the two ends | | **Who may send work** | Whatever the server code allows | Closed by default; allow and trust lists | | **Untrusted work** | Left to the implementer | Sandbox without network or model key | | **Payment** | a2a-x402 with its own facilitator | a2a-x402 built in, with signed prices and limits | | **Proof of what happened** | Not specified | Provider-signed receipts, verified offline | ANet needs a hub, and the hub sees traffic metadata.
